teaching.hint: Which portions of the array can never lose value under a leftward move?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Every original prefix sum is a lower bound on its final sum, so its ceiling average bounds the maximum; these bounds are jointly attainable.
solution_outline.approach: Compute the maximum ceiling average among all original prefixes. To justify attainability at a target maximum, carry forced excess from right to left and show feasibility is equivalent to every prefix average meeting that target.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: A running sum holds each original prefix total. The best bound after index i is the largest ceiling prefix average seen so far.
solution_outline.correctness: Any final maximum x implies each prefix total is at most its length times x. Conversely the minimum forced right-to-left carry fits at index zero exactly when all those inequalities hold. The largest ceiling average is therefore both necessary and sufficient.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space; the running sum may reach 10^14 and needs wide arithmetic.
solution_outline.pitfall: Using only the whole-array average ignores an overloaded prefix that cannot send units right.

source_fidelity_notes: Kept directional operation and numeric limits; removed procedural example.
